STATE OF NEW HAMPSHIRE




                                 OFFICE OF LEGISLATIVE SERVICES
                                      ADMINISTRATIVE RULES
                                       STATE HOUSE ANNEX
                                  25 CAPITOL STREET, ROOM 234
                                       CONCORD, NH 03301




Rulemaking Notice Form

Notice Number: 2026-194

Rule Number: Agr 2500


   1. Agency: Department of Agriculture, Markets, and Food
      Agency Address: Department of Agriculture, Markets, and Food
                      Office of the Commissioner
                      One Granite Place, Ste 211
                      Concord, NH 03301

   2. RSA Authority: RSA 433:22

   3. Federal Authority:

   4. Action(s): Readopt w/Amendment

   5. Short Title: Nursery and Nursery Stock

   6. (a) Summary of what the rule says and of any proposed amendments including
      whether the rule implements a state statute for the first time:

              The proposed rule readopts and substantively amends the Agr 2500 Nursery and
      Nursery Stock rules. The revision modernizes and reorganizes the regulatory framework
      governing the licensing, inspection, certification, quarantine, and enforcement
      requirements for nurseries, plant dealers, landscapers, and other entities handling nursery
      stock. Major amendments include expanded and restructured definitions aligned with RSA
      terminology; a redesigned licensing framework establishing an electronic application and
      renewal system; new application timelines and late-fee provisions; detailed inspection
      authorities including references to prohibited invasive species lists; a fully rewritten
      quarantine section with expanded operational requirements; updated procedures for
      interstate and international certification via the federal phytosanitary certificate issuance
      and tracking(PCIT) system; and expanded enforcement provisions addressing violations
      such as false information, obstruction, and failure to pay fees. Minor amendments include
      organizational changes, clarifying edits, updated statutory citations, and alignment of
      terminology.



ADMINISTRATIVE RULES (603) 271-3680                                    Generated on 09/18/2026
             _ Does this rule implement a state statute for the first time?

            The proposed rule does not implement a statute for the first time.

  6. (b) Brief description of the groups affected:

             The proposed rules affect nurseries, plant dealers, landscapers, and other
     businesses that grow, store, sell, distribute, or ship nursery stock within or from New
     Hampshire. Entities engaged in interstate or international shipment of nursery stock will
     be affected by updated certification requirements. Businesses located within or handling
     regulated articles from quarantine areas will be subject to expanded quarantine
     compliance obligations. Independently owned businesses with annual gross sales of
     rooted plant material will be affected by revised licensing fees and new electronic licensing
     procedures, including deadlines and late fee requirements. State agencies and
     universities exchanging nursery stock, as well as not for profit arboreta, remain exempt
     from licensing fees.

  6. (c) Specific section or sections of state statute or federal statute or regulation which
     the rule is intended to implement:

        Provision of the Proposed            Specific State or Federal Statute or
                  Rule                    Regulations which the Rule is Intended to
                                                         Implement
      Agr 2501.01-Agr 2501.02            RSA 433:21; RSA 433:24; RSA 433:27
      Agr 2501.03                        RSA 433:22, II, V, VII; RSA 433:27; RSA
                                         433:29-a;
      Agr 2501.04                        RSA 433:22, II, VII
      Agr 2501.05                        RSA 433:22, III, VII; RSA 433:25
      Agr 2501.06                        RSA 433:22, II, IV, VII; RSA 433:25;
      Agr 2501.07                        RSA 433:21; RSA 433:22, VII; RSA 433:23
      Agr 2502.01                        RSA 433:23; RSA 433:26; RSA 433:28; RSA
                                         433:29; RSA 433:29-a; RSA 433:30; RSA
                                         433:33, RSA 430:53
      Agr 2503.01                        RSA 433:22, VI; RSA 433:24; RSA 433:30,
                                         RSA 433:34
      Agr 2504.01                        RSA 433:22, III, IV, VII; RSA 433:23 RSA
                                         433:24; RSA 433:25; RSA 433:30
      Agr 2505.01                        RSA 433:31; RSA 433:32; RSA 433:33, RSA
                                         433:34; RSA 433:35; RSA 433:36




ADMINISTRATIVE RULES (603) 271-3680                                    Generated on 09/18/2026
   7. Contact person for copies and questions including requests to accommodate
     persons with disabilities:

                                               Title: Director, Division of Plant
      Name: Piera Siegert
                                               Industry
      Address: Department of Agriculture,
      Markets, and Food
      Division of Plant Industry               Phone Number: (603) 271-2561
      29 Hazen Drive
      Concord, NH 03301
                                               FAX Number:
                                               Email: piera.y.siegert@agr.nh.gov

  8. Deadline for submission of materials in writing or, if practicable for the agency, in
     the electronic format specified:

     Thursday, November 12, 2026

     _ Fax
     X Email piera.y.siegert@agr.nh.gov
     _ Other

  9. Public hearing scheduled for:
     Date: Wednesday, November 4, 2026
     Time: 10:00 AM
     Place: Dept. Agriculture, Markets, and Food
            One Granite Place, Room 202
            Concord, NH 03301

     Electronic Access, if applicable: N/A

  10. Fiscal Impact Statement (Prepared by Legislative Budget Assistant):

         FIS #: 26: 192, dated: Friday, September 11, 2026

     1. Comparison of the costs of the proposed rule(s) to the existing rule(s):

        When compared to the existing rules, the proposed rules will increase State revenues
     and increase costs for certain independently owned businesses.

     2. Cite the Federal mandate. Identify the impact on state funds:

         No federal mandate, no impact on state funds

     3. Cost and benefits of the proposed rule(s):

         The proposed rules increase the annual plant dealer licensing fee from $25 to $50 for
     licensees with annual gross sales greater than $3,000 and establish a $25 annual
     licensing fee for licensees with annual gross sales of $3,000 or less, who are currently
     exempt from the licensing fee. Based on 792 licensees with annual gross sales greater
     than $3,000, the $25 fee increase may result in an additional $19,800 in annual revenue

ADMINISTRATIVE RULES (603) 271-3680                                  Generated on 09/18/2026
      (792 x $25). Based on 187 licensees with annual gross sales of $3,000 or less, the new
     $25 fee may result in an additional $4,675 in annual revenue (187 x $25). Therefore, the
     proposed fee changes may increase State revenue by approximately $24,475 annually
     ($19,800 + $4,675). Actual revenue may vary based on the number of licensed plant
     dealers, particularly among those with annual gross sales of $3,000 or less, as there is
     significant volatility among these low-volume sellers.

         A. To State general or State special funds:

            The proposed rule may increase General Fund revenue by $25,000 annually.

         B. To State citizens and political subdivisions:

            None.

         C. To independently owned businesses:

            The proposed rules will increase costs for certain independently owned businesses
         who are required to get a plant dealer’s license.

  11. Statement Relative to Part I, Article 28-a of the N.H. Constitution:

            These rules do not violate Part I, Article 28-a of the NH Constitution because the
     rules neither mandate, expand, nor assign any responsibility or cost to any political
     subdivision.




ADMINISTRATIVE RULES (603) 271-3680                                 Generated on 09/18/2026
